category_title: Failing students who reject observation tasks and provide emotional feedback
minimal_context: The student is preparing to play a set of seven points in badminton against a partner and needs to declare a strategic target zone before starting.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Before you start this set of seven points, you need to declare your strategic project. Which target zone are you aiming for on the court?

STUDENT: (Hits the shuttlecock directly to the central zone of the opposing court) I'm just hitting it to the middle.

TUTOR: The task is to choose a specific zone, like the front or the back, before you play.

STUDENT: Why do I have to tell him my plan? He's my opponent. I don't see the point of this pair work.

TUTOR: Please just declare your strategic project so we can continue the lesson.

STUDENT: No, I'm not declaring any project. This is stupid and I'm not doing it.

options.A: Direct the student to just go and play the set of seven points for a bit, and then discuss the strategic project afterward.
options.B: Ask the student to think of one additional strategic project to focus on if the initial target zone is not enough.
options.C: Physically mark the badminton court into three zones and focus instruction on hitting to the 'danger zones' (front and back thirds).
options.D: Provide reinforcement (e.g., school tickets and behavior-specific praise) for declaring a strategic project and sharing evidence of using it during the set.
